memory_lessons.applicability: Use only as same-target evidence when choosing a tile size; it does not establish a general tile-size rule.
memory_lessons.claim: The 128-element streaming variant was valid at 106.05 µs, while the 256-element variant was valid at 69.73 µs in the supplied measurements. The smaller tile was slower in those runs.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the 512-element tile under the same official protocol and compare its correctness and timing with the 256-element result.

proposal.hypothesis: Against the measured 256-element tile (69.73 µs), a 512-element tile halves tile-loop iterations on wide rows and may reduce loop overhead; its larger live tile state could instead hurt occupancy or register use. The 128-element variant measured slower at 106.05 µs, so official measurement must determine whether this larger tile helps without sacrificing correctness on tails.

retained: Changed the compile-time column tile from 256 to 512 elements while retaining stable running-maximum and rescaled-sum accumulation.
Retained masked handling for arbitrary row widths and tails, input strides, and the second tiled pass for normalized output.
